text:
Victor Eklund was the 16th pick last June, played one NHL game last season, and has now scored in three straight for the Islanders, including a power-play goal in San Jose. Six goals in 17 games at 20 years old, and the ice time is rising, up to almost 15 minutes a night and 18 in his last game.

He plays a physical game: 52 hits, the most of anyone in this batch. Brayden Schenn, his linemate, called him tenacious to NHL.com's Stefen Rosner, someone who "goes to hard areas, wins battles." The Islanders have slightly better chance share with him than without him.

The goals are running ahead of the chances. He is shooting 23% on 4.43 expected goals, and the team has scored nearly five more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. Among forwards drafted 11th to 21st since 2005, the median first full season is 0.32 points a game; he is at 0.53. His rookie range is wide. The physical game and the minutes are what look real so far.
headline: Victor Eklund has made the Islanders' lineup his own
